messages:
laura: Heads-up: found two related advisories that affect our go services: CVE-2024-9999 (grpc net/http denial vector in proxy handling) and CVE-2024-10101 (golang-jwt token validation edgecase). Can we risk-rank and decide if this needs a hotpatch or rolling deploy next week?

arpit: Thanks — can you paste the dependency tree and which services are on which versions? quick note: jwt lib in auth-service is v3.x, grpc is v1.50 on most services.

laura: auth-service go.mod excerpt:```
module github.com/redwood/auth-service

require (
  github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v3.2.1+incompatible
  google.golang.org/grpc v1.50.0
)
```
only a couple of edge internal services pinned to older grpc (v1.48).

mike: My quick read — CVE-2024-10101 affects JWT parsing for certain compressed claims where signature validation could be bypassed in v3.x. v4.0.0 has the fix but includes some API changes (ParseWithClaims signature).

carmen: For grpc CVE the call-site is the proxy layer that handles HTTP/2 framing; risk is medium-high if customers use our external proxy. We should test rolling grpc v1.51+ which has the fix.

arpit: Proposed triage:
- Risk: jwt CVE = high for token-issuing/auth services; grpc CVE = medium for edge proxies.
- Action: emergency patch for auth-service (pin to github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.0.0) with integration tests + canary.
- grpc: schedule a staged rollout (canary -> region -> global) next maintenance window unless exploit seen.

laura: Agree. Also need to check KMS signing integration: we use Cloud KMS to sign JWTs via detached go wrapper. v4 jwt changed header handling — please ensure our signing flow still calls Sign/Verify correctly.

mike: I tested locally: wrapper snippet still works but we must update usage from `jwt.Parse` to `jwt.ParseWithClaims` where we rely on custom claims unmarshal. I'll open a PR with minimal changes.

carmen: Audit logging: any emergency patch must include a migration note in audit logs and an event that records library upgrade + who approved. Ops requires an RBAC temporary role for the patch runners.

laura: For compliance I want: PR link, changelog entry, KMS key rotation plan (if signing semantics changed), and a post-deploy validation script that checks token acceptance.

mike: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/512 (draft) — includes jwt v4 pin, updated tests, and a small shim:```
func ParseToken(tok string) (*Claims, error) {
  return jwt.ParseWithClaims(tok, &Claims{}, keyFunc)
}
```
CI passes locally.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline passed for PR 512 — all unit and integration tests green.

arpit: Next steps and owners:
- mike: finalize PR + add rollback test (owner)
- carmen: schedule canary in staging and run audit-log entry (owner)
- laura: approve emergency release and notify compliance
- ops: temporary RBAC role: "dep-hotpatcher" valid for 48h

carmen: I'll create the audit event: `audit:event lib-upgrade service=auth-service from=github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v3.2.1 to=github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v4.0.0 approved_by=laura`

laura: Approving now. Please include a short postmortem if anything breaks.

mike: For grpc, I'll prepare a compatibility matrix and a smoke test for streaming RPCs. Plan: canary 5% traffic in region-1, watch for increased reconnections.

arpit: Also: add a dependency pin check in CI that fails if transitive deps bring older grpc/jwt versions. We had a slip-through last time.

laura: Thanks team. If anyone finds a vulnerable public PoC, escalate to SEV-1. Otherwise follow the canary + staged rollout plan.

carmen: Logging note: make sure the patch job emits an audit log record for KMS usage during signing test runs (we'll need that for compliance sampling).

mike: Will add test that signs tokens via KMS using the rotated key alias and assert Verify succeeds.

laura: Closing loop — I'll post the final timeline in #incidents if we go hot. Otherwise we'll aim for next-week staged deployment. :thumbsup:
